We don't need to do a `.get()` to compare with `nullptr`
the .get() method returns a raw pointer to the managed object. This raw pointer can then be compared with nullptr to check if the smart pointer is currently managing an object or if it is "empty."
The comparison with `nullptr` can be done with the smart pointer object itself.
I don't see any downside in using get?
